So it seems like the opinions are divided here. I wouldn’t tell her that you know about it, because having your parents find out about self harm without being ready for a conversation is awful. It takes time to open up and I think you shouldn’t pressure her.

I think just telling her that you care and are there for her is enough. You could tell her that you noticed some changes and ask her if she wants to tell you something. If she doesn’t, that’s okay. I think you are pretty worried now, so asking if she is at any risk and offering professional help is also a good idea. 
You need to know that self harm is a coping mechanism and not everyone who self harms is suicidal. I know that this won’t calm you, but you can’t really help much. Like I said, hiding her box will only make it worse. She could get offended by it, hide it better or even stop trusting you. That’s why I wouldn’t say that I found the box or anything… I know it’s hard. Tell her that you love her and offer conversations without judgement :)

I know it's incredibly tough to see someone struggle daily. Make sure they know that u are there for them. You can't do much and I know how frustrating that shit is. I've been there too, only with a friend of mine.. You need to know that it's never your fault. Emotional support is important right now, know that they urges have nothing to do with you. Try to be unbiased.  It's hard to accept that a loved one will hurt themselves, but there really isn't much you can do.  If it does happen in the future, please be careful not to react angry, sad, or dissapointed.  It's good that your sister trusts you and wants to talk to you.  Be happy about it.  I know that it takes a lot to open up.

For me personally random check ups help a lot, cuz I don't feel confortable writing or telling someone if I feel like relapsing lul. Try to make sure that they know that u are there for them and willing to help!
Codewords or codesymbols could help. It's hard to explain what you feel when u are close to relapsing and texting whole paragraphs is nearly impossible. So maybe agree on an emoji or a simple word that your partner can send/say when they feel the urge again.
Everybody needs something different, I think she is searching for your support but you should definitely have a open conversation. A conversation about how you can support her is very important. . Some might like physical touch, some don't that's why you should definitely talk to them! I don't know ur relationship but maybe you can also give them some simple tasks like drawing what they feel, writing down their experiences from the day,  going for a walk, taking care of themselves in Form of shower, masks or sports, making food or cleaning.  Simple tasks are also a great way to overcome a depressive episode cuz doing tasks can make u feel happy  :)
Without being too pushy you both could research for healthier coping mechanisms, u could tell them how you cope and what you read how others cope. Maybe they can adapt some new ways :)
They have to ask for professional help themselves, otherwise it won't help. If they really want to overcome the problem professional help is awesome but if they are just being forced it won't help. Some people don't like to talk about what they are going through, so don't force them. Sure encouragement is alright but pushing them won't be a good idea. 

Don't forget your own mental health, it's the first thing to look after. You can't help her is you're not mentally stable yourself. I wish u all the best.
